# Introduction

This workflow selects variants, constructs gene/region haplotypes and examines
LD before phenotype association. It uses the deterministic data described in
[Getting started](getting-started.html#demo-data). Package website:
<https://renscq.github.io/GeneTrackR/>.

# Read and inspect variants {#variants}

```{r read-variants}
library(GeneTrackR)

demo_dir <- system.file("extdata", package = "GeneTrackR")
vcf_file <- file.path(demo_dir, "gtr_demo_variants.vcf")
gp <- read_genepred(
  file.path(demo_dir, "gtr_demo.genePredExt"),
  format = "genePredExt",
  verbose = FALSE,
  progress = FALSE
)
vcf <- read_vcf(
  vcf_file,
  mode = "memory",
  keep_genotype = TRUE,
  verbose = FALSE,
  progress = FALSE
)
summary_vcf(vcf)
validate_vcf(vcf)$invalid_summary
```

VariantTrack stores variants at 1-based point positions (`start == end == pos`).
REF, ALT, INFO, FORMAT and sample columns are available for inspection; raw
sample fields are not a replacement for VariantAnnotation's typed VCF model.
An indel's GRanges export remains a point projection, not its reference-allele
span. Match genome assembly, chromosome names and sample identifiers before
combining external annotations.

```{r query-variants}
gene_variants <- retrieve_vcf(
  vcf,
  annotation = gp,
  gene_id = "GeneA",
  as = "VariantTrack",
  verbose = FALSE
)
variant_table <- as.data.frame(gene_variants$data)
variant_table[c("variant_id", "chrom", "pos", "ref", "alt")]

selected <- retrieve_vcf(
  vcf,
  variant_id = c("varA03", "varA04"),
  verbose = FALSE
)
selected$variant_id
variant_ranges <- as_granges(gene_variants)
head(variant_ranges)

figure_style <- ggplot2::theme(
  text = ggplot2::element_text(
    family = "Arial",
    colour = "black",
    face = "plain"
  )
)
plot_variant(
  gene_variants,
  chrom = "chr1",
  start = 12339001L,
  end = 12352000L,
  text_size = 9
) +
  ggplot2::theme_classic(base_family = "Arial") +
  figure_style +
  ggplot2::theme(axis.text = ggplot2::element_text(colour = "black"))
```

Regional `read_vcf()` calls require `chrom`, `start` and `end` together.
`retrieve_vcf()` also accepts `chrom` alone to select an entire chromosome;
use all three arguments for a bounded interval.
Gene/transcript queries resolve their range from annotation; upstream and
downstream flanks follow strand when `strand_aware = TRUE`. Do not combine a
gene/transcript locator with a separate coordinate range. Type and text filters
can be applied without an interval; see `?retrieve_vcf` for matching rules.

## Indexed regional access

`mode = "auto"` creates a lazy VariantTrack when an index is present and no
region is supplied. Lazy indexed regional queries reuse Rsamtools. A complete
region can also be supplied directly to `read_vcf()`. Requesting lazy mode
without an index produces the documented warning and memory fallback.

The bundled plain VCF is intentionally suitable for small in-memory examples.
For real indexed files, validate sample names and the returned region just as
for memory mode. Filters that need the whole file can require full reading.
Do not infer an empty file from a regional query returning zero records.

## Start with a standard VCF object

If a workflow starts with a `VariantAnnotation` `CollapsedVCF`, use
`as_variant_track()` to run GeneTrackR's POS-based queries. The original ranges,
typed fields and header remain available for selection through `as_vcf()`.
For large inputs, use `VariantAnnotation::ScanVcfParam()` with an indexed VCF
to load the region before adapting it.

```{r standard-vcf-input, eval=requireNamespace("VariantAnnotation", quietly=TRUE)}
standard_vcf <- VariantAnnotation::readVcf(vcf_file, genome = NA_character_)
standard_track <- as_variant_track(standard_vcf)
standard_gene <- retrieve_vcf(
  standard_track,
  annotation = gp,
  gene_id = "GeneA",
  as = "VariantTrack",
  verbose = FALSE
)
standard_subset <- as_vcf(standard_gene, samples = c("S02", "S01"))
head(VariantAnnotation::geno(standard_subset)$GT)
```

The adapter associates records by source row, so repeated positions or IDs
can be selected and exported. Use unique variant IDs for haplotype construction,
which reshapes the genotype table by variant ID. See
[Export results](export-results.html#typed-vcf-export) for genotype-aware export.

# Construct and inspect haplotypes

```{r haplotypes}
hap <- hap_gene_variant(
  vcf,
  annotation = gp,
  gene_id = "GeneA",
  genotype_mode = "string",
  min_variant_number = 1
)
hap$haplotypes
head(hap$sample_haplotypes)

plot_hap_variant(
  hap,
  annotation = gp,
  min_hap_samples = 3,
  variant_label = "pos",
  gene_track_legend_position = "top",
  text_size = 9
) & figure_style
```

A HapVariant links selected variants, genotype tables, haplotype definitions
and sample assignments. Inspect these tables before interpreting a plot.
Genotype encoding, missing calls, heterozygosity and multiallelic inputs can
affect grouping. `genotype_mode` and filtering arguments are explicit analysis
choices; retain them with the result. Raw phase separators in VCF fields do
not by themselves prove that a downstream grouping is a phased haplotype model.

`hap_region_variant()` provides the coordinate-region entry. Gene/transcript
entries add annotation-aware location and plotting context. Specialized label,
reference-row, genotype and sample-filter controls are documented in the
corresponding function help, without a second duplicated tutorial.

# Examine linkage disequilibrium {#ld}

LD is a relationship between observed genotype patterns. It provides context
for correlated association signals and does not identify a causal site.
The example uses the existing `r2` method and its documented genotype handling.

```{r ld-gradient}
ld <- compute_ld_block(
  vcf,
  chrom = "chr1",
  start = 12342620L,
  end = 12355500L,
  variant_type = "snp",
  method = "r2",
  verbose = FALSE
)
head(ld$data)

plot_ld_block(
  ld,
  annotation = gp,
  show_region = TRUE,
  show_variant_labels = FALSE,
  font = 9,
  return_object = FALSE
) & figure_style
```

The twelve designed variants form 66 pairs. The perfect six-variant core
contributes fifteen pairs at high LD; weaker downstream relationships provide
a gradient. Inspect the numerical matrix/table together with the triangle.
For actual data, report sample inclusion, missingness, method and variant
filters alongside the displayed LD values.

```{r ld-two-variants, fig.height=4}
pair <- compute_ld_block(
  vcf,
  chrom = "chr2",
  start = 16995001L,
  end = 17006000L,
  method = "r2",
  verbose = FALSE
)
pair$data
```

`plot_ld_block()` normally returns the updated LDTrack with `$figure`; use
`return_object = FALSE` when a figure alone is required. Keep variants, matrix
and region information together when exporting an analysis.

Continue with [phenotype comparisons and refinement](phenotype.html). For
integrated signal/variant/gene displays, use the [complete workflow](complete-workflow.html).
